mainTopic: Child rules for יבום and תרומה, the close of יש מותרות, and the new משנה about a woman whose husband returns
overview: This amud opens by finishing a צריכותא, which explains why the תורה needs both "כנעוריה" and "זרע אין לה" for a כהן's daughter who wants to go back to eating תרומה. Next comes a series of קל וחומר arguments comparing יבום and תרומה. They ask whether a dead child counts like a living one, and whether a child from another husband counts. Each argument is blocked, either by "דרכיה דרכי נעם" or by the exact words of a פסוק. That closes פרק יש מותרות. A new פרק then opens with a משנה about a woman who remarried after hearing her husband died, and then he came back. She must leave both men, loses her marriage rights, and her children are ממזרים, though רבי יוסי, רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון disagree on some points. The משנה also shows that a בית דין's ruling frees her from a קרבן. The גמרא then tries to prove that one witness is believed about a husband's death, bringing several sources. The last source, the ברייתא on "או הודע אליו," read as a case of one witness who says "you ate חלב," is challenged with the idea that silence counts as admitting. That discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Finishing why both phrases are needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes explaining why the תורה needs both "כנעוריה" and "זרע אין לה". Each phrase teaches a case that the other phrase would not cover.
steps.simpleTranslation: "As in her youth" rules out a pregnant woman, since her body was empty before and is full now. But for a woman who already gave birth, her body was empty before and is empty again now. You might think she can still eat תרומה, so the phrase "she has no child" is needed for her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an answer it began on the previous amud (87a). It shows that each of the two phrases in the פסוק teaches something the other does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "כנעוריה" only rules out a pregnant woman, because her body has changed from how it was in her youth. A woman who already gave birth looks the same as before, so we might wrongly let her eat תרומה. The phrase "זרע אין לה" is needed to rule her out too.

keyTerms.meaning: it is necessary, so both phrases are needed

steps.whatToRemember: "כנעוריה" rules out a pregnant woman. "זרע אין לה" rules out a woman who has already given birth. The תורה needs both.

phrases.english: was empty, and now her body is full.
phrases.notes: This picks up mid-sentence from the previous amud: "at the beginning her body" was empty. He's talking about a pregnant woman.

phrases.english: But regarding "she has no child,"
where at the beginning her body was empty
and now her body is also empty,
you might say she is not disqualified; therefore it is necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the צריכותא that began on the previous amud.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both phrases are needed. "כנעוריה" covers a pregnant woman, and "זרע אין לה" covers a woman who has already given birth.

steps.title: A memory-aid list for the coming discussions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a short list of key words to help remember the order of the discussions that follow.
steps.simpleTranslation: Memory aid: "Said to him, we should not make," "her deeds," "by death," "we should make and not make," "by a child," "יבם and תרומה," "יבום and תרומה."
steps.whatsHappening: This line is not an argument. It is setting up the next discussions by listing their key words so we can remember their order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word in the list comes from the opening or main phrase of one of the coming exchanges. The list points ahead to arguments about יבום and תרומה, about dead children compared to living ones, and about a child from the first husband compared to one from the second.

keyTerms.meaning: a memory aid made of key words
levirate marriage, when a man marries his brother's widow
the priestly portion of produce, which only a כהן's household may eat

phrases.english: Mnemonic: (Said to him), we should not make,
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out "אמר ליה" in round brackets. The whole memory aid is in square brackets, so it's wording the corrected text adds.

phrases.english: her deeds, by death,
we should make and not make, by a child,
yavam and teruma,
levirate marriage and teruma: this is the mnemonic.

steps.title: רב יהודה's argument that dead children should not count like living ones
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה מדאסקרתא challenges רבא with a קל וחומר from תרומה to יבום. By this logic, a child who died should not exempt his mother from יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה מדאסקרתא said to רבא: we should prove that dead children are not like living ones for יבום, using a קל וחומר. For תרומה, a child from the first husband counts like a child from the second, and he disqualifies her from eating תרומה. Even there, a dead child is not treated like a living one. For יבום, a child from the first husband does not count like one from the second to exempt her. So surely there a dead child should not be treated like a living one!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה is attacking the rule that a child who dies still exempts his mother from יבום. He builds a קל וחומר to argue against it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For תרומה, the law reaches widely and even counts a child from a different husband. Yet even there, a dead child does not count. יבום is narrower and only counts the late husband's own child. So it seems even more likely that a dead child should not count there, and then the יבמה should still need יבום.

keyTerms.meaning: treating dead children as if they were living

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב יְהוּדָה מִדִּאסְקַרְתָּא לְרָבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda from De'iskarta said to Rava:
Should we not make the dead like the living?
with regard to levirate marriage, by a "how much more so" argument:

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה בְּמָקוֹם שֶׁעָשָׂה וָלָד מִן הָרִאשׁוֹן
phrases.english: If in a place where the Torah made a child from the first husband
like a child from the second husband
to disqualify her from eating teruma,
it still did not make dead children like living ones;

phrases.aramaic: מָקוֹם שֶׁלֹּא עָשָׂה וָלָד מִן הָרִאשׁוֹן
phrases.english: then in a place where it did not make a child from the first husband

phrases.aramaic: כְּוָלָד מִן הַשֵּׁנִי לְפוֹטְרָהּ מִן הַיִּיבּוּם —
phrases.english: like a child from the second, to exempt her from levirate marriage,

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ דִּין שֶׁלֹּא נַעֲשֶׂה מֵתִים כְּחַיִּים?!
phrases.english: is it not logical that we should not make the dead like the living?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב יְהוּדָה מִדִּאסְקַרְתָּא לְרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new discussion about the ברייתא's rules for children, as the memory aid previewed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a child who was alive when his father died, and died afterward, still exempts his mother from יבום.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר. תרומה is the broader law, yet even there dead children are not counted. So in יבום, the narrower law, they should certainly not be counted.

steps.title: The Torah's ways are pleasant
steps.stepSummary: The קל וחומר is answered with the פסוק "her ways are ways of pleasantness". The תורה would not create a law that harms a woman's peaceful married life.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: "Her ways are ways of pleasantness, and all her paths are peace."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב יהודה's argument with a פסוק from משלי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose the child died after she had already married someone else. If she then needed יבום or חליצה, it could shame her in front of her new husband and damage her marriage. The תורה's ways are pleasant, so it would not create such a law. That is why she stays exempt, even though the קל וחומר seemed to say otherwise.
steps.whatToRemember: A dead child still exempts his mother from יבום. Logic alone might say otherwise, but the תורה's ways are pleasant and would not ruin her new marriage.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that "דרכיה דרכי נעם" can actually decide a הלכה, even outweighing a קל וחומר.

phrases.english: The verse states:
"Her ways are ways of pleasantness,"
phrases.notes: משלי 3:17

phrases.english: "and all her paths are peace."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יהודה's קל וחומר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A פסוק that overrides the logical argument
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Based on the קל וחומר, a dead child should not exempt her, so she would need יבום.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because the תורה's ways are pleasant, she stays exempt and is not pulled away from a new marriage.

steps.title: Should a dead child keep her from eating תרומה, as it does in יבום?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a קל וחומר: יבום counts a child who has since died, so תרומה should count one too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us treat a dead child like a living one for תרומה, using a קל וחומר. In יבום the תורה is stricter about which child counts: a child from a first husband does not free her. Yet even there, a child who later died still counts. In תרומה the תורה is more generous: even a child from a first husband counts to keep her from eating. Surely there a dead child should count too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא builds a קל וחומר to argue that a dead child should stop a כהן's daughter from going back to eat תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יבום is narrow in one way: only the dead husband's own child counts. Yet it is broad in another way: a child who died later still counts. תרומה is already broader about which child counts, since any husband's child counts. So the argument says תרומה should also be broad about dead children.

keyTerms.meaning: An argument from a weaker case to a stronger case: if it is true there, surely it is true here.
Treating children who died as if they were still alive.
A child from the woman's first husband, a different man.
The holy portion of produce given to כהנים, eaten by them and their household.
Is it not logical? The phrase that closes a קל וחומר.

steps.confusionAlert: Each case here has two separate questions. First, does a child from another husband count? Second, does a child who died count? יבום and תרומה answer these two questions in opposite ways, and every קל וחומר in this section plays them against each other.

phrases.english: And let us make dead children like living ones with regard to תרומה
from a קל וחומר:
And if in a place where the תורה did not make

phrases.aramaic: וָלָד מִן הָרִאשׁוֹן כְּוָלָד מִן הַשֵּׁנִי
phrases.english: a child from the first husband like a child from the second
phrases.notes: "The second" here is the husband who died, whose child would free her from יבום.

phrases.english: to exempt her from יבום
it still made dead children like living ones;

phrases.aramaic: מָקוֹם שֶׁעָשָׂה וָלָד מִן הָרִאשׁוֹן כְּוָלָד מִן הַשֵּׁנִי
phrases.english: then in a place where it did make a child from the first like a child from the second
to disqualify her from eating תרומה
is it not logical that we should make dead children like living ones?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְנַעֲשָׂה מֵתִים כְּחַיִּים לְעִנְיַן תְּרוּמָה מִקַּל וְחוֹמֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the קל וחומר from תרומה to יבום was blocked, the גמרא now tries the opposite direction, from יבום to תרומה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a dead child does not prevent a כהן's daughter from going back to eat תרומה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: יבום is stricter about which child counts but still counts dead children. So תרומה, which is more generous about which child counts, should certainly count dead children.

steps.title: The פסוק says she has no child, and right now she has none
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק "וזרע אין לה" is in the present tense, so only a living child counts for תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says "and she has no child." Right now, she has none.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא blocks the קל וחומר with the wording of the פסוק about תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "אין לה" means she has no child at this moment. A child who already died is not someone she has now, so she may go back to eating תרומה. A פסוק overrides a קל וחומר.

keyTerms.meaning: Therefore the פסוק teaches; it introduces a verse that settles the question.
And look, she does not have one.

phrases.english: The verse states: "and she has no child,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:13

phrases.english: and she does not have one now.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״וְזֶרַע אֵין לָהּ״, וְהָא אֵין לָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קל וחומר of step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A פסוק blocks the קל וחומר.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A dead child should count for תרומה just as it does for יבום.
steps.terutzMaskana: For תרומה, only a child who is alive now counts.

steps.title: Should a child from another husband free her from יבום, as it does in תרומה?
steps.stepSummary: A second קל וחומר: תרומה counts a child from any husband, so יבום should too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us treat a child from her first husband like a child from the dead husband for יבום, using a קל וחומר. In תרומה the תורה does not count dead children, yet it does count a child from any husband. In יבום the תורה does count dead children. Surely there a child from another husband should count too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא flips the comparison and tries to bring the תרומה rule about any husband's child into יבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now תרומה is the weaker case, because it does not count dead children. Even so, it counts a child from a different husband. יבום is broader about dead children, so the argument says it should also be broad about a different husband's child and free the widow from יבום.

keyTerms.meaning: Levirate marriage: a brother marries the widow of his brother who died without children.
Where the תורה did not make, meaning did not treat this way.

phrases.aramaic: וְנַעֲשֶׂה וָלָד מִן הָרִאשׁוֹן כְּוָלָד מִן הַשֵּׁנִי
phrases.english: And let us make a child from the first husband like a child from the second
with regard to יבום, from a קל וחומר:

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה בְּמָקוֹם שֶׁלֹּא עָשָׂה מֵתִים כְּחַיִּים
phrases.english: And if in a place where the תורה did not make dead children like living ones
with regard to תרומה

phrases.aramaic: — עָשָׂה וָלָד מִן הָרִאשׁוֹן כְּוָלָד מִן הַשֵּׁנִי;
phrases.english: it still made a child from the first like a child from the second;

phrases.aramaic: מָקוֹם שֶׁעָשָׂה מֵתִים כְּחַיִּים לְעִנְיַן יִבּוּם
phrases.english: then in a place where it did make dead children like living ones, with regard to יבום

phrases.aramaic: — אֵינוֹ דִּין שֶׁנַּעֲשֶׂה וָלָד מִן הָרִאשׁוֹן כְּוָלָד מִן הַשֵּׁנִי?!
phrases.english: is it not logical that we should make a child from the first like a child from the second?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְנַעֲשֶׂה וָלָד מִן הָרִאשׁוֹן כְּוָלָד מִן הַשֵּׁנִי לְעִנְיַן יִבּוּם מִקַּל וְחוֹמֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same two rules as step 5, but argues from תרומה to יבום.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that only the dead husband's own child frees his widow from יבום.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: תרומה is narrower about dead children but still counts any husband's child. So יבום, which is broader about dead children, should surely count any husband's child.

steps.title: The פסוק says he has no son, and he had none
steps.stepSummary: The יבום פסוק is about the dead man's own child, so her child from another man does not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says "and he has no son," and he, the dead husband, had none.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא blocks the second קל וחומר by pointing out that the יבום פסוק speaks about the man's child.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words are "אין לו", meaning he has none, not "she has none." What matters for יבום is whether the dead brother left a child. Her child from a different man is not his child.

keyTerms.meaning: "And he has no son": the condition for יבום.

phrases.english: The verse states: "and he has no son,"
phrases.notes: דברים 25:5

phrases.english: and he does not have one.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״וּבֵן אֵין לוֹ״, וְהָא אֵין לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קל וחומר of step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A פסוק blocks the קל וחומר.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Her child from a first husband should free her from יבום.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the dead husband's own child frees her, because the פסוק says "he" has no son.

steps.title: Should a child from another husband not count for תרומה, as in יבום?
steps.stepSummary: A third קל וחומר: יבום ignores a child from another husband, so תרומה should ignore that child too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say a child from her first husband does not count for תרומה, using a קל וחומר. In יבום the תורה counts dead children, yet it ignores a child from another husband. In תרומה the תורה does not count dead children. Surely there a child from another husband should not count either!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one last direction: bringing the יבום rule that ignores another husband's child into תרומה, which would let her eat תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here יבום is the broader case, because it counts dead children. Even so, it does not count another man's child. תרומה is narrower about dead children, so the argument says it should surely not count another man's child either.

keyTerms.meaning: And let us not make, meaning not treat as the same.

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא נַעֲשֶׂה וָלָד מִן הָרִאשׁוֹן כְּוָלָד מִן הַשֵּׁנִי
phrases.english: And let us not make a child from the first husband like a child from the second
for תרומה, from a קל וחומר:
If in a place where the תורה did make dead children like living ones
to exempt her from יבום

phrases.aramaic: — לֹא עָשָׂה וָלָד מִן הָרִאשׁוֹן כְּוָלָד מִן הַשֵּׁנִי;
phrases.english: it did not make a child from the first like a child from the second;

phrases.aramaic: מָקוֹם שֶׁלֹּא עָשָׂה מֵתִים כְּחַיִּים לְעִנְיַן תְּרוּמָה
phrases.english: then in a place where it did not make dead children like living ones, with regard to תרומה

phrases.aramaic: — אֵינוֹ דִּין שֶׁלֹּא נַעֲשֶׂה וָלָד מִן הָרִאשׁוֹן כְּוָלָד מִן הַשֵּׁנִי?!
phrases.english: is it not logical that we should not make a child from the first like a child from the second?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא נַעֲשֶׂה וָלָד מִן הָרִאשׁוֹן כְּוָלָד מִן הַשֵּׁנִי לִתְרוּמָה מִקַּל וְחוֹמֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same two rules again, now arguing from יבום to תרומה about another husband's child.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a child from any husband keeps a כהן's daughter from going back to eat תרומה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: יבום is broader about dead children but still ignores another man's child. So תרומה, which is narrower about dead children, should surely ignore another man's child.

steps.title: The פסוק says she has no child, but she does have one
steps.stepSummary: The תרומה פסוק looks only at whether she has a child, so a child from any husband counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says "she has no child," but she does have one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא blocks the third קל וחומר by reading the תרומה פסוק plainly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says "אין לה", meaning she has none, without naming any particular husband. So any living child of hers counts, whoever the father is, and she may not go back to eating תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: But look, she does have one.

steps.whatToRemember: Every rule here comes from the exact words of the פסוקים. In תרומה, "אין לה" asks whether she has a living child now, from any husband. In יבום, "אין לו" asks whether the dead man left a child, even one who died later. A פסוק always beats a קל וחומר.
steps.whyThisMatters: These three blocked arguments, together with the one in steps 3 and 4, show that the two areas of law cannot be mixed. Each has its own definition of having a child, fixed by its own פסוק.

phrases.english: The verse states: "she has no child,"
phrases.notes: Same פסוק as before, ויקרא 22:13, now stressing "to her": any child of hers counts.

phrases.english: but she does have one.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״אֵין לָהּ״, וְהָא יֵשׁ לָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קל וחומר of step 9 and ends the series.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A פסוק blocks the קל וחומר.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Her child from a first husband should not keep her from eating תרומה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Any living child of hers, from any husband, keeps her from going back to eat תרומה.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing the chapter יש מותרות
steps.stepSummary: The closing line of the פרק יש מותרות.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק יש מותרות.
steps.whatsHappening: This line marks the end of the chapter called יש מותרות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is the traditional closing words said when finishing a פרק. It adds no new law, and the next chapter begins after it.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you: the formula said on finishing a פרק.

phrases.english: We will return to you, יש מותרות

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after the final answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The פרק יש מותרות is complete.

steps.title: The case: the husband comes back after she remarried
steps.stepSummary: A woman remarries after hearing her husband died. When he returns alive, she must leave both men, and each must give her a גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a woman's husband went overseas, and people told her he had died, and she married someone else, and then her first husband came back, she must leave both men. She also needs a גט from each of them.
steps.whatsHappening: A new פרק opens with a new משנה. It describes the case and gives the first ruling: she must separate from both husbands and get a גט from each.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She did not do anything on purpose, since she relied on a report. Even so, the משנה does not let her stay with either man. It also requires a גט from the second man, even though her marriage to him was never a real marriage, because she was still married to the first.

keyTerms.meaning: She must leave (separate from the husband)
From this one and from that one (both husbands)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think she may go back to the first husband because she did nothing wrong on purpose. The משנה says she must leave both of them.
steps.whyThisMatters: This opening case is the foundation for every other rule in the משנה. Each later penalty is about this same woman.

phrases.english: A woman whose husband went overseas
and people came and told her, "Your husband died"
and she remarried, and afterward her husband came back
she must leave this one and that one
and she needs a divorce document from this one and from that one

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new פרק after the previous פרק closed in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman who remarried on a false report of her husband's death must leave both men and needs a גט from each.

steps.title: She loses all her money rights from both men
steps.stepSummary: She gets no כתובה, no profits, no food support, and no worn clothing from either man. If she already took any of these, she must give it back.
steps.simpleTranslation: She has no כתובה, no profits, no food support, and no worn-out clothing, not from this man and not from that man. If she took anything from either one, she must return it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists the money and property rights that a wife normally has. It says she loses all of them, with both men.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A normal wife who is divorced or widowed collects her כתובה and other benefits. Here she gets nothing from the first husband or from the second. The rule even reaches backward: anything she already collected must be returned.

keyTerms.meaning: The marriage contract payment a wife receives at divorce or widowhood
Worn-out clothing or items she brought into the marriage

phrases.english: And she has no marriage contract payment
nor profits, nor food support
phrases.notes: Profits here means what the husbands earned from her property. She can't demand that back.

phrases.english: nor worn-out clothing

phrases.aramaic: לֹא עַל זֶה וְלֹא עַל זֶה
phrases.english: not from this one and not from that one
And if she took from this one or from that one
she must return it

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה, adding money penalties to the separation ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: She loses her כתובה, profits, food support and worn clothing from both men, and must return anything she took.

steps.title: Her children, burial impurity, and the husbands' rights
steps.stepSummary: A child from either man is a ממזר. Neither man may become טמא for her, and neither has a husband's rights to her found items, earnings, or vows.
steps.simpleTranslation: A child from either man is a ממזר. Neither man may become impure for her. Neither man has a right to what she finds, to what she earns, or to cancel her vows.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה keeps listing results. First it covers her children, and then it shows that neither man is treated as her husband in any way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A child from the second man is a ממזר because she was still married to the first. The משנה also says this about the first husband. A husband who is a כהן may become טמא to bury his wife, and a husband normally owns her found items and earnings and can cancel her vows. Here both men lose all of these rights.

keyTerms.meaning: A child born from a forbidden relationship, who may not marry into the regular community
Becomes ritually impure (a כהן doing so for a close relative's burial)
Canceling vows, a right a husband normally has

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think only the second man's child is a ממזר. The משנה says מזה ומזה, so even a child from the first husband after this is a ממזר.

phrases.english: And the child is a mamzer from this one and from that one
And neither this one nor that one becomes impure for her
phrases.notes: This is talking about when the men are כהנים and she dies.

phrases.english: And neither this one nor that one is entitled
not to her found items, nor to her earnings
nor to canceling her vows

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of consequences, moving from her money rights to her children and the husbands' rights.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Children from either man are ממזרים, and neither man has any husband's rights toward her.

steps.title: Lost status, no inheritance of her כתובה, and only חליצה
steps.stepSummary: She becomes disqualified from כהונה, from מעשר, or from תרומה, depending on her family. Neither man's heirs inherit her כתובה. If the men die, their brothers do חליצה, not יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she was a בת ישראל, she may no longer marry a כהן. A Levite's daughter loses מעשר, and a כהן's daughter loses תרומה. The heirs of neither man inherit her כתובה. If the men died, the brothers of each one do חליצה and not יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes its list. It covers her status, inheritance, and what happens with the husbands' brothers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her relationship with the second man counts as a forbidden one, so she loses the special status she had through her father's family. Because neither man counts as her real husband, his heirs do not inherit her כתובה. For the same reason, after each man dies his brother may not do יבום. Only חליצה is done.

keyTerms.meaning: The priesthood (here, being allowed to marry a כהן)

steps.whatToRemember: The whole משנה follows one idea: once she remarried while her first husband was alive, neither man is treated as her real husband. She leaves both, loses every marriage benefit, her children are ממזרים, and the brothers may only do חליצה.
steps.whyThisMatters: The גמרא will go on to explain the line about the heirs and her כתובה. This list sets up the whole discussion of the פרק.

phrases.english: If she was a regular Israelite woman
she is disqualified from the priesthood
phrases.notes: He means she may no longer marry a כהן.

phrases.english: and a Levite's daughter, from the tithe
and a priest's daughter, from teruma

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין יוֹרְשִׁין שֶׁל זֶה וְיוֹרְשִׁין שֶׁל זֶה
phrases.english: And neither the heirs of this one nor the heirs of that one
inherit her marriage contract payment
And if they died
phrases.notes: This is talking about when the men died without children.

phrases.aramaic: אָחִיו שֶׁל זֶה וְאָחִיו שֶׁל זֶה
phrases.english: the brother of this one and the brother of that one
do the release ceremony, and do not do levirate marriage

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיְתָה בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל נִפְסְלָה מִן הַכְּהוּנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the list of consequences in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: She loses her כהונה, מעשר, or תרומה status. Neither man's heirs inherit her כתובה, and the brothers do only חליצה, not יבום.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: her כתובה still rests on the first husband's property
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי disagrees with the earlier rule that she gets no כתובה. He holds that her כתובה is still owed from the first husband's property.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: her כתובה is a claim on her first husband's property.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings רבי יוסי, who argues with one of the penalties listed before. He says she does not lose her כתובה from the first husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 said she gets no כתובה from either man. רבי יוסי says the first husband's property still stands behind her כתובה. So he softens the penalty only for the first husband, who was her real, original husband.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
her כתובה is on the property of her first husband.
phrases.notes: He is arguing with Step 13, which said she gets no כתובה at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A dissenting view against the penalty in Step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Her כתובה remains a claim on the first husband's estate.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: the first husband keeps a husband's rights
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר holds that the first husband still gets her found items and her earnings, and he can still cancel her vows.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר says: the first husband is entitled to what she finds and what she earns, and to cancel her vows.
steps.whatsHappening: Another תנא argues with the earlier list. רבי אלעזר says the first husband keeps his rights as a husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 said neither man has rights to her found items, earnings or vows. רבי אלעזר says the first husband does keep these rights. Her second marriage was a mistake, so the first husband does not lose what he had as her husband.

keyTerms.meaning: her earnings (the work of her hands)

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar says:
the first husband is entitled to her found items
phrases.notes: This argues with Step 14, which took these rights away from both men.

phrases.english: and to her earnings, and to cancelling her vows.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second dissent, this time against Step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first husband retains rights to her finds, her earnings, and annulment of her vows.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: her ביאה or חליצה frees her co-wife, and her child is not a ממזר
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון holds that if the first husband's brother does יבום or חליצה with her, this frees her co-wife. He also holds that a child from the first husband is not a ממזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: her relations or her חליצה with the first husband's brother frees her co-wife. And a child from him is not a ממזר.
steps.whatsHappening: A third תנא argues with the earlier penalties. רבי שמעון treats her as still a full wife of the first husband in two ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 said the brothers do חליצה but not יבום. רבי שמעון says that either her ביאה or her חליצה with the first husband's brother works fully, so her צרה is freed too. Step 14 called a child from either man a ממזר. רבי שמעון says a child from the first husband is not a ממזר.
steps.confusionAlert: 'From him' (מִמֶּנּוּ) means the first husband, not the second. A child from the second husband is still a ממזר.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
her relations or her חליצה
with the brother of the first husband
frees her co-wife.
And the child from him is not a ממזר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third dissent, against Steps 14 and 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Her יבום or חליצה with the first husband's brother frees her co-wife, and a child from the first husband is not a ממזר.

steps.title: Without permission she may return, and with בית דין she owes no קרבן
steps.stepSummary: If she remarried 'without permission', she may go back to the first husband. If she remarried by order of a בית דין, she must leave but owes no קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she married without permission, she may return to him. If she married by order of the court, she must leave, and she is exempt from bringing a קרבן.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now shows that all the harsh rules above apply only in certain cases. It contrasts a marriage 'without permission' with one done by order of a בית דין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Without permission' is surprising here, because she is allowed to go back to her husband. The גמרא will explain that it means she did not need the court because she had two witnesses. When a בית דין allowed her to marry, she must leave, but she is free from a חטאת because she relied on the court.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'without permission' as wrongdoing. The גמרא (Step 22) explains that she simply did not need the court's permission because she had full witnesses.

phrases.english: And if she married without permission,
she is permitted to return to him.
phrases.notes: 'Him' is the first husband, who came back alive.

phrases.english: If she married by order of the court,
she must leave, and she is exempt from the offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the penalties of Steps 12 to 15 by setting out different cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Without permission she may return. With a בית דין's permission she must leave but owes no קרבן.

steps.title: Without a בית דין she owes a קרבן, which shows the court's power
steps.stepSummary: If she remarried without a court's ruling, she must leave and owes a קרבן. The court's ruling is strong enough to free her from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she did not marry by order of the court, she must leave and must bring a קרבן. The court's power is greater, because it frees her from the קרבן.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the opposite case and then states the lesson: a ruling from בית דין protects her from having to bring a קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without the court, she acted on her own mistaken judgment, so she owes a חטאת for unknowingly sinning. A court's ruling makes her count as forced into the mistake, so she is exempt.

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נִיסֵּת עַל פִּי בֵּית דִּין —
phrases.english: If she did not marry by order of the court,
she must leave, and she is obligated to bring an offering.
The power of the court is greater,
since it frees her from the offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא נִיסֵּת עַל פִּי בֵּית דִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the contrasting case to Step 19 and draws the lesson.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Without a בית דין she owes a קרבן. The court's ruling frees her from it.

steps.title: The court allowed marriage, not wrongful relations
steps.stepSummary: If the court allowed her to remarry and she instead had relations outside marriage, she owes a קרבן. The court permitted only marriage.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the court told her she could marry, and she went and did wrong, she must bring a קרבן, because they only permitted her to marry.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה sets a limit on the court's protection. It covers only what the court actually allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The court's ruling frees her from a קרבן only for a marriage. Relations outside of marriage were never permitted, so for those she is like anyone who sinned by mistake, and she owes a חטאת.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's main lesson: a בית דין ruling saves her from a קרבן, but only for exactly what the court allowed, which is marriage.

phrases.english: If the court ruled that she may marry,
and she went and did wrong,
phrases.notes: He means she had relations with a man without marrying him.

phrases.english: she is obligated to bring an offering,
since they permitted her only to marry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the exemption given in Step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The court's exemption covers only marriage, not relations outside marriage.

steps.title: The גמרא reads the end of the משנה: 'without permission' means with witnesses
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that 'without permission' in the סיפא means she did not need the court, because she had two witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the end of the משנה teaches, 'If she married without permission, she may return to him,' that must mean without the court's permission but with witnesses.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins. It reads the end of the משנה closely to set up a proof, which comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Why would a woman who married 'without permission' be allowed back to her husband? Because she had two proper witnesses, so she never needed the court, and she was completely misled by them. This reading of the סיפא sets up what the רישא must mean.

keyTerms.meaning: the Talmud's discussion of the משנה

phrases.english: גמרא: Since the last part teaches:
If she married without permission,
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה from Step 19.

phrases.english: she is permitted to return to him,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא בִּרְשׁוּת בֵּית דִּין, אֶלָּא בְּעֵדִים.
phrases.english: that means not with the court's permission, but with witnesses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא by reading the משנה's סיפא.
steps.raayaObject: Sets up the proof that one witness is believed.

steps.title: So the first case had one witness, which shows one witness is believed
steps.stepSummary: From the סיפא, the גמרא infers that the רישא, where she needed the court, involved only one witness. So a court lets her remarry based on one witness.
steps.simpleTranslation: This implies that the first part is with the court's permission and with one witness. Apparently, one witness is believed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its proof. It concludes from the משנה that עד אחד is believed about a husband's death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the סיפא is the case of two witnesses, then the רישא, where she needed the court's permission, must be a case with fewer than two witnesses, meaning one. Since the court did permit her to remarry there, a single witness must be enough.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a key source that a woman may remarry on the word of עד אחד, which is unlike most areas of הלכה, where two witnesses are needed.

phrases.english: It follows that the first part is with the court's permission,
and with one witness.
Apparently, one witness is believed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the inference set up in Step 22.
steps.raayaObject: That one witness is believed about a husband's death.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The contrast between the רישא and the סיפא of the משנה.

steps.title: Proof from the custom of allowing remarriage on hearsay
steps.stepSummary: A משנה says the practice was to let a woman remarry even on hearsay testimony, and even through a woman or a slave. This shows one witness is believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: We also learned: they became accustomed to letting a woman remarry based on a witness quoting another witness, a woman quoting a woman, or a woman quoting a male or female slave. So one witness is believed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another משנה to support the idea that one witness is believed. In that משנה, people normally not fit to testify are enough to let a woman remarry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In regular court cases, hearsay, women and slaves cannot testify. Here, though, they are enough to establish that a husband died. If even such weak testimony works, then a single proper witness surely counts.

keyTerms.meaning: They became established; it became the accepted practice
A witness repeating what another witness said (hearsay)

phrases.english: And we also learned: they became accustomed to allowing remarriage

phrases.aramaic: עֵד מִפִּי עֵד, וְאִשָּׁה מִפִּי אִשָּׁה,
phrases.english: based on a witness quoting a witness, and a woman quoting a woman,
and a woman quoting a male slave or a female slave.
Apparently, one witness is believed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second proof to the conclusion of step 23 that one witness is enough.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה that allows remarriage on hearsay from a woman or a slave

steps.title: Proof from one witness who says 'you ate חלב'
steps.stepSummary: A משנה exempts a person from a קרבן only when he denies one witness's claim. If he stays silent, the witness is believed, so one witness is trusted מדאורייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: We also learned: if one witness says 'you ate חלב' and he says 'I did not eat,' he is exempt. He is exempt only because he denied it. If he stayed silent, the witness is believed. So one witness is believed by Torah law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third משנה, about forbidden fat (חלב). It reads that משנה closely to show that one witness is trusted even by Torah law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only says he is exempt when he denies it. The גמרא infers the flip side: if he says nothing, he must bring a קרבן based on one witness. A קרבן is a Torah obligation, so this proof goes further than the earlier ones. It shows one witness counts מדאורייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden fat; eating it by accident requires a חַטָּאת

phrases.aramaic: וּתְנַן נָמֵי: עֵד אֶחָד אוֹמֵר ״אָכַלְתָּ חֵלֶב״,
phrases.english: And we also learned: one witness says 'You ate forbidden fat,'
and he says 'I did not eat' — he is exempt.
The reason is that he said 'I did not eat,'
but if he stayed silent, the witness is believed.
Apparently, one witness is believed by Torah law.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּתְנַן נָמֵי: עֵד אֶחָד אוֹמֵר ״אָכַלְתָּ חֵלֶב״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A stronger proof: it shows one witness is believed even by Torah law.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about one witness who says 'you ate חלב,' read for what happens when he stays silent

steps.title: Asking for the Torah source
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where in the Torah we learn that one witness is believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the Torah source of the rule from the last step. It is setting up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 25 said one witness is believed מדאורייתא. A Torah-level rule needs a source in a פסוק, so the גמרא now looks for one.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this?

phrases.english: From where do we derive this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the Torah source of the conclusion in step 25.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק showing that one witness is believed by Torah law

steps.title: The ברייתא on 'או הודע אליו חטאתו'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads the פסוק to say others cannot obligate him if he denies it. Still, if he does not deny it, he must bring the קרבן whatever way he found out.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: 'Or his sin be made known to him' means he himself must know, not that others inform him. You might think he is exempt even if he does not deny it. So the פסוק says 'or it be made known to him': in any way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא that explains the פסוק about bringing a חטאת. The ברייתא learns two things from the same words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First, the ברייתא says others cannot make him bring a קרבן against his own word. Then it adds that if he does not deny their claim, he must bring it, however he learned of the sin. That second point is what the גמרא will now use.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Or his sin be made known to him' (the פסוק about bringing a חטאת)
He contradicts him (denies the witness's claim)
In any case / however it happens

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא: 'Or his sin be made known to him.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:23

phrases.english: And not that others make it known to him.

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ מַכְחִישׁוֹ
phrases.english: I might have thought that even if he does not contradict him
he should be exempt?
The פסוק teaches: 'Or it be made known to him' —
in any case.
phrases.notes: However he finds out, if he does not deny it, he must bring the קרבן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 26 with a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'או הודע אליו' teaches that he must bring the קרבן if he does not deny what he was told.

steps.title: The ברייתא must be about one witness
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows the ברייתא cannot be about two witnesses, because then no פסוק would be needed. So it is about one witness, and that witness is believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If two witnesses came and he does not contradict them, why do I need a פסוק? Rather, it must be one witness, and when he does not contradict him, the witness is believed. Learn from this that one witness is believed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא works out what case the ברייתא is talking about. It concludes that the case is one witness, which proves one witness is believed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two witnesses are always believed, so a פסוק would add nothing in that case. A פסוק is needed only to teach something new, which here is that one witness counts. This turns the ברייתא into a Torah source for the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What are the circumstances?
Why do I need a פסוק?

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?
If we say that two witnesses came
and he does not contradict them,
why do I need a פסוק?
phrases.notes: Two witnesses are always believed, so a פסוק would teach nothing new.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not about one witness,

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי לָא קָא מַכְחִישׁ לֵיהּ — מְהֵימַן,
phrases.english: and when he does not contradict him, the witness is believed?
Learn from this that one witness is believed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the ברייתא from step 27 to pull out the proof.
steps.raayaObject: One witness is believed by Torah law
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא on 'או הודע אליו,' which only makes sense if it is about one witness

steps.title: Maybe his silence is the reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the proof. Maybe he brings the קרבן because his silence counts as admitting it, not because the witness is believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do you know the reason is that the witness is believed? Perhaps it is because he stays silent, and silence is like an admission.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from the last step. It offers a different reason why he must bring the קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling is the same, but the reason changes. If silence counts as admitting, then the obligation comes from him, not from the witness. In that case the ברייתא proves nothing about trusting one witness.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying he goes free when he stays silent. He still brings the קרבן. The only question is why: because the witness is trusted, or because he admitted it by staying quiet.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next part of the סוגיא: step 30 uses the end of the same ברייתא to show that silence really is the reason.

phrases.english: And from where do you know that it is because the witness is believed?
Perhaps it is because he is silent,
and silence is like an admission?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 28 and also weakens the inference of step 25.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the ברייתא and the חלב משנה that one witness is believed מדאורייתא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The obligation may come from his silence counting as an admission, not from trusting the witness.

steps.title: Even two witnesses cannot obligate him if he denies it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports its rejection from step 29. The end of the ברייתא says that if two witnesses say he ate חלב and he denies it, he is exempt from a קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can see this is true from the end of the משנה: if two witnesses say, "You ate חלב," and he says, "I did not eat it," he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for its point that the קרבן depends on the person's own word. If he denies it, even two witnesses cannot obligate him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally two witnesses decide any case. Here they cannot make him bring a קרבן against his own denial. So the קרבן clearly depends on what he himself accepts. That means in the first part, with one witness, he brings it because his silence counts as admitting, not because one witness is believed.

keyTerms.meaning: "Know it"; you can see this is true. It introduces support for a point.
The last part of a משנה or ברייתא
Forbidden fat. Eating it by mistake requires a חטאת offering.

steps.confusionAlert: This is not saying two witnesses are weak in general. It is only saying that for a קרבן, the person's own denial controls the outcome.

phrases.english: Know that it is so, for the latter clause teaches:
phrases.notes: The latter clause is the end of the same ברייתא from step 27.

phrases.english: If two witnesses said, "You ate forbidden fat,"
and he says, "I did not eat it,"
he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the rejection in step 29, which said his silence works like an admission.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the קרבן depends on the sinner's own acceptance, not on how believable the witness is
steps.raayaSupportSource: The end of the ברייתא: two witnesses against his denial leave him exempt

steps.title: רבי מאיר holds him liable using a קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר disagrees and holds him liable. If two witnesses can bring a person to the death penalty, they should surely be able to obligate him in a lighter קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר holds him liable. רבי מאיר said: It is a קל וחומר. If two witnesses can bring him to the severe death penalty, shouldn't they be able to bring him to the lighter obligation of a קרבן?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with רבי מאיר, who disagrees with the ruling that he is exempt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר reasons from the more severe case to the lighter one. Witnesses can have a person put to death even if he denies the act. So they should also be able to obligate him in a קרבן, which is much lighter.

keyTerms.meaning: Reasoning from a lighter case to a more severe one, or the reverse
An offering; here, a חטאת for eating חלב by mistake

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir holds him liable.
Rabbi Meir said: It is an a fortiori argument:
If two witnesses can bring him
to the severe penalty of death,
shall they not bring him to the lighter obligation of an offering?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי מֵאִיר מְחַיֵּיב. אָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר: קַל וָחוֹמֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the disagreeing view inside the same משנה (from step 25) quoted in step 30.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: two witnesses obligate him in a קרבן even if he denies it, by קל וחומר from the death penalty.

steps.title: The חכמים answer: he could claim he sinned on purpose
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים reject רבי מאיר's קל וחומר. He could always say "I did it on purpose," and then he would not bring a קרבן anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: What if he wants to say, "I did it on purpose"!
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים answer רבי מאיר and explain why a קרבן is different from the death penalty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קרבן is only brought for a sin done by mistake. If he says he sinned on purpose, the witnesses cannot make him bring one. Since his own words can free him from the קרבן that way, he can also free himself by denying the act. Death works differently, because his denial does not change it.

keyTerms.meaning: On purpose; deliberately. A deliberate sinner does not bring a חטאת.

steps.whatToRemember: According to the חכמים, the person's own word controls whether he brings a קרבן. Even two witnesses cannot force it against his denial.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the end of the ברייתא supports step 29: the קרבן depends on his own word, so the first part may also be about his silence and not about trusting one witness.

phrases.english: They said to him:
What if he wants to say,
"I did it on purpose"!
phrases.notes: A person who sins on purpose brings no חטאת. So by saying this, he could get out of the קרבן anyway.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: מָה אִם יִרְצֶה לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי מאיר's קל וחומר from step 31.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבי מאיר's comparison between the death penalty and a קרבן
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A קרבן can always be avoided by his own claim that he sinned on purpose. The death penalty cannot be avoided that way, so the comparison fails.

steps.title: Turning back to the first clause
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to look again at the first part of the משנה. The full move continues in the next lines.
steps.simpleTranslation: The first clause...
steps.whatsHappening: This one word is a setup. The גמרא is turning back to the first part of the משנה to explain it, and the explanation comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the end of the משנה showed that his own word controls the קרבן, the גמרא now returns to the first part, the case of one witness. The question of whether one witness is believed will be looked at again there.

keyTerms.meaning: The first part of a משנה or ברייתא

phrases.english: The first clause...
phrases.notes: The sentence keeps going in the next part of the דף. Here the גמרא is just pointing back to the start of the ברייתא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the end of the ברייתא, the גמרא returns to its first part.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How to understand the first part of the ברייתא, the case of one witness, given what the end of the ברייתא showed
